newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine interest rates seen consolidating.
newsitem.headline: Philippine interest rates seen consolidating.

text.p: Philippine interest rates are seen consolidating at current levels as banks await further indications of a possible rise in U.S. interest rates, traders said on Monday.
The U.S. Federal Open Market Committee meets on Tuesday amid increasing speculation interest rates will be raised.

On Monday, the Philippine benchmark 91-day Treasury bill rate nudged down to single-digit levels for the second consecutive week after the Central Bank cut its key overnight borrowing rate twice two weeks ago by a total of 0.4375 percentage to 10 percent.
The 91-day T-bill rate slipped to 9.724 percent from last week's 9.804; the 182-day fell to 9.969 from 10.134 percent; and the 364-day rate edged down to 10.517 from 10.638 percent.
The 91-day and 182-day rates were last in single-digit levels in September 1995 and October 1994 respectively.
Traders said they did not expect the Central Bank to make a move on its key rate until a decision on U.S. rates is out.
"By bringing its rate down, it would be more like gambling especially if there is a hike in U.S. interest rates," a dealer from a foreign bank said.
The trader was referring to the Central Bank's cutting of its key rate two weeks ago which led to a brief weakening of the peso.

In an interview with Reuters after the Treasury bill auction on Monday, Deputy Treasurer Eduardo Mendiola said he expects interest rates to continue to slip in the coming weeks amid a low inflation scenario and liquidity in the system.
"It will be sideways to slightly down," he said.
Far East Bank President Octavio Espiritu said "for as long as inflation remains low...I would expect interest rates to remain low."

Year-on-year inflation slackened to 4.4 percent in February from 5.0 percent in January. The government expects inflation this year to slow down to six to seven percent this year from 8.4 percent last year.
Despite the low-interest rate scenario, Espiritu said he expected the peso to remain stable.

"We do not see any major fluctuation in foreign exchange rate, We have sufficient (international) reserves. There is continued inflow of direct investment, portfolio investment. We expect stability," Espiritu said.
